q.e: A line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side shows the three angles lying on a straight line.

q.t: Two angles of a triangle are 60° and 80°. Find the third (in degrees).
An exterior angle of a triangle equals:
o: The sum of the two interior opposite angles
q.e: Exterior + adjacent interior = 180° = sum of all three interior angles.

In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles add up to:
q.e: The right angle uses 90° of the 180°.

q.t: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are:
q.e: The triangle is symmetric about its axis.

q.t: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one interior opposite angle is 50°. Find the other (in degrees).
Can all three angles of a triangle be less than 60°?
o: No — the sum would be less than 180°

q.t: The angles of a triangle are x°, x° and 2x°. Find the largest (in degrees).
A triangle can have at most how many obtuse angles?
q.e: Two obtuse angles would already exceed 180°.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. Find the largest (in degrees).
An exterior angle of a triangle is 125° and the interior opposite angles are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the larger of them (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠A + ∠B = 125° and ∠A + ∠C = 113°. Find ∠A (in degrees).
The angles of a triangle are (x − 40)°, (x − 20)° and (x/2 − 10)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 80°. Find each base angle (in degrees).
The three exterior angles of a triangle (one at each vertex) add up to:
q.e: Three linear pairs total 540°; removing the interior 180° leaves 360°.

q.t: In a right-angled triangle one acute angle is twice the other. Find the smaller (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠A = 60°. The bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O. Find ∠BOC (in degrees).
q.e: ∠BOC = 90° + ½∠A, because the halves of ∠B and ∠C add to ½(180 − 60) = 60°.

q.t: Find each exterior angle of an equilateral triangle (in degrees).
In a triangle, one angle is 90° and another is 37°. Find the third (in degrees).
q.e: The two acute angles add to 90°.

q.t: In △ABC, ∠A − ∠B = 15° and ∠B − ∠C = 30°. Find ∠A (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠A = 70°. The bisectors of the EXTERIOR angles at B and C meet at O. Find ∠BOC (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠A = 2∠B = 6∠C. Find ∠A (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠B = 60° and ∠C = 40°. AD is the altitude and AE the bisector of ∠A. Find ∠DAE (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A = 80°, so ∠BAE = 40°. In right △ABD, ∠BAD = 30°. The difference is 10° — always ½(∠B − ∠C).

q.t: Two angles of a triangle add up to 116° and differ by 24°. Find the smallest angle of the triangle (in degrees).
q.e: The two are 70° and 46°; the third is 64°.

q.t: In △ABC the exterior angle at C is 130° and ∠A = ∠B. Find ∠A (in degrees).
The angles of a triangle are three consecutive even numbers of degrees. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: The middle one is 180 ÷ 3 = 60: the angles are 58°, 60°, 62°.

q.t: One angle of a triangle equals the sum of the other two. The triangle is:
In △ABC, ∠A = 50° and the exterior angle at B is 115°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠B = 45° and ∠C = 55°. The bisector of ∠A meets BC at D. Find ∠ADC (in degrees).
q.e: ∠A = 80°, so ∠BAD = 40°. ∠ADC is an exterior angle of △ABD: 45 + 40.

q.t: Find the sum of the angles at the five points of a five-pointed star (in degrees).
q.e: Using exterior angles, the five tip angles fit into one triangle’s angle sum: 180°.

q.t: In △ABC, AD bisects ∠A and is also perpendicular to BC. ∠A = 100°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
D is a point on side BC of △ABC with AD = BD = CD. Find ∠BAC (in degrees).
In △ABC, AB = AC. D is a point on AC with BD = BC = AD. Find ∠A (in degrees).
q.e: Let ∠A = x. Then ∠ABD = x, ∠BDC = 2x = ∠C = ∠B. So x + 2x + 2x = 180.

q.t: Side BC of △ABC is produced both ways. The exterior angles at B and C are 110° and 125°. Find ∠A (in degrees).
In △ABC, ∠A = 70°. The bisector of ∠B and the bisector of the EXTERIOR angle at C meet at D. Find ∠BDC (in degrees).
q.e: Half the exterior angle at C = ½(∠A + ∠B). Subtracting ½∠B leaves ½∠A.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are (5x − 60)°, (2x + 40)° and (3x − 80)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
One angle of a triangle is 130°. Find the angle between the bisectors of the other two angles (in degrees).
The exterior angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find its smallest INTERIOR angle (in degrees).
q.e: Exterior angles: 80°, 120°, 160°. The largest exterior angle goes with the smallest interior: 20°.

q.t: In △ABC, ∠A = 72° and ∠B = 2∠C. Find ∠B (in degrees).
